Vendor shall not charge for work outside scope that Customer did not approve in a signed change order.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-5","number":"5","heading":"IMPLEMENTATION AND CHANGE CONTROL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-5.1","number":"5.1","heading":"Vendor shall prepare and maintain an implementation plan identifying tasks, owners, assumptions, dependencies, deliverables, acceptance criteria, risks, and target dates. The Parties will hold regular status meetings during implementation. Vendor shall keep accurate action and decision logs and furnish them to Customer on request.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6","number":"6","heading":"ACCEPTANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6.1","number":"6.1","heading":"Customer will have fifteen business days after delivery of a Deliverable to test it against the acceptance criteria in the applicable Order Form. Customer may accept it in writing or reject it by describing material nonconformities. Payment, productive use needed for testing, or silence does not constitute acceptance.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6.2","number":"6.2","heading":"If Customer rejects a Deliverable, Vendor shall promptly correct the nonconformities at no additional charge and resubmit it for a new acceptance period. After two unsuccessful correction cycles, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and receive a refund of Fees paid for the rejected Deliverable and dependent Services Customer cannot reasonably use.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7","number":"7","heading":"FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.1","number":"7.1","heading":"Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.2","number":"7.2","heading":"Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.2-2","number":"7.2","heading":"Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.3","number":"7.3","heading":"Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.4","number":"7.4","heading":"Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.5","number":"7.5","heading":"Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.6","number":"7.6","heading":"Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8","number":"8","heading":"TERM AND RENEWAL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.1","number":"8.1","heading":"This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.2","number":"8.2","heading":"Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.3","number":"8.3","heading":"On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9","number":"9","heading":"TERMINATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.1","number":"9.1","heading":"Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.2","number":"9.2","heading":"Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.3","number":"9.3","heading":"Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.5","number":"9.5","heading":"Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10","number":"10","heading":"EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10.1","number":"10.1","heading":"On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10.2","number":"10.2","heading":"Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-11","number":"11","heading":"TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND DATA RETURN","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-11.1","number":"11.1","heading":"Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-11.2","number":"11.2","heading":"Within thirty days after Customer's request, Vendor shall return all Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with relationships and metadata reasonably necessary for use. Vendor shall not withhold Customer Data because of a fee dispute.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-11.3","number":"11.3","heading":"After Customer confirms successful return, Vendor shall securely delete remaining Customer Data from active systems and, as backups cycle, from backups, except for a copy required by Applicable Law. An authorized officer shall certify deletion in writing. Any retained copy remains protected and may not be used for another purpose.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12","number":"12","heading":"CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12.3","number":"12.3","heading":"Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12.4","number":"12.4","heading":"For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13","number":"13","heading":"ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.1","number":"13.1","heading":"Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.2","number":"13.2","heading":"For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.3","number":"13.3","heading":"Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.4","number":"13.4","heading":"Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14","number":"14","heading":"INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.1","number":"14.1","heading":"As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.2","number":"14.2","heading":"Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.3","number":"14.3","heading":"Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.4","number":"14.4","heading":"No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15","number":"15","heading":"CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15.1","number":"15.1","heading":"Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, to provide the Services, and as permitted by this Agreement. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data, use it for advertising, combine it with another customer's identifiable data, or train a generally available model on it without Customer's express written consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15.2","number":"15.2","heading":"Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law concerning personal information. If Vendor processes personal information for Customer, the Parties' data-processing addendum is incorporated. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16","number":"16","heading":"CONFIDENTIALITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.1","number":"16.1","heading":"“Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.2","number":"16.2","heading":"The recipient shall use Confidential Information only to perform or exercise rights under this Agreement, protect it with at least reasonable care, and disclose it only to personnel, Affiliates, advisers, and subcontractors who need to know and are bound by confidentiality obligations. The recipient is responsible for their unauthorized use or disclosure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.5","number":"16.5","heading":"On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17","number":"17","heading":"INFORMATION SECURITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17.1","number":"17.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain a written information-security program using administrative, technical, organizational, and physical safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of Customer Data and risk. Notice will include known facts, affected data and systems, containment, and a contact.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18","number":"18","heading":"INSURANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.1","number":"18.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.2","number":"18.2","heading":"Policies will be issued by reputable insurers and be primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary. On request, Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance and evidence of relevant coverage. Vendor shall give advance notice of cancellation or material reduction to the extent available from its insurer. Insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19","number":"19","heading":"WARRANTIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.1","number":"19.1","heading":"Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.2","number":"19.2","heading":"For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.3","number":"19.3","heading":"Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. input.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a sole-and-exclusive supplier obligation, and this clause contradicts Sections 2.1 and 12.3, so we have deleted it. If Vendor needs protection we could discuss exclusivity limited to a defined product category for 12 months, ending automatically if Vendor misses service levels.
input.summary: Delete Customer exclusivity obligation in 2.2.

input.comment: [Playbook] We do not give most-favoured-customer undertakings to suppliers, and this clause is inconsistent with Section 12.3, so we have deleted it. MFN pricing running in our favour remains welcome.
input.summary: Delete Customer-side MFN in 7.2.

ops.oldText: Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
ops.newText: If Customer materially delays a dependency identified in an Order Form, Vendor is relieved of the affected obligations and dates for the period of delay and may recover its documented, reasonable additional time-and-materials costs actually incurred as a result. No liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer.

input.comment: [Playbook] We do not pay liquidated damages or penalties; USD 25,000 per day for any dependency delay is punitive and uncapped. We have replaced it with schedule relief plus Vendor's documented additional costs, which is the standard remedy for customer-caused delay.
input.summary: Replace Customer-payable liquidated damages with schedule relief and documented costs.

ops.oldText: unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice
ops.newText: unless either Party gives thirty days' advance written notice before the end of the then-current term, and Vendor shall remind Customer of the upcoming renewal at least sixty days before it occurs

input.comment: [Playbook] A 180-day non-renewal window is far longer than we can operate; our position is a 30-day opt-out with a 60-day Vendor reminder (fallback: 60 days). The 12-month renewal term and the Section 8.3 uplift cap of the lesser of CPI and 3% are acceptable.
input.summary: Shorten non-renewal notice from 180 to 30 days and add renewal reminder.

ops.oldText: For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
ops.newText: For twelve months after a person's involvement in the Services ends, neither Party will knowingly solicit for employment any of the other Party's personnel who were directly involved in performing or receiving the Services. This does not restrict general advertisements or other recruitment not targeted at the other Party's personnel, responses to them, or the hiring of any person who approaches a Party on an unsolicited basis, and neither Party is restricted from hiring any person.

input.comment: [Playbook] We accept only a mutual, narrow non-solicit: 12 months from the end of a person's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire. The 18-month, all-personnel, "engage" restriction binding only us is not acceptable and conflicts with Section 12.3.
input.summary: Make non-solicit mutual, 12 months, involved personnel only, with carve-outs and no no-hire.

ops.oldText: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
ops.newText: No more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice and during normal business hours, Vendor may engage an independent auditor bound by confidentiality obligations to verify Customer's usage of the Services by reviewing relevant usage records Customer provides. Vendor and its auditor have no right of access to Customer's systems, whether remote or on-site.

input.comment: [Playbook] Audits of our usage must be no more than annual, on 30 days' notice, records-based and conducted by an independent auditor, with no access to our systems. As drafted, unlimited unannounced audits with remote system access is a walk-away and already contradicts the access limits in Section 22.2.
input.summary: Limit audits to annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, records only, no system access.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty or early-termination charge, in which case Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination in accordance with Section 10.2. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

input.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 contains no convenience right, which we cannot accept in a three-year term (Section 8.1). We have added a Customer-only termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund keyed to Section 10.2; our fallback is 60-90 days' notice.
input.summary: Insert Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund.

input.rationale: Matches our preferred position: mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees (paid or payable) and USD 1,000,000; mutual consequential-damages exclusion in 21.2 with incident-response and replacement-service costs preserved as direct damages; Excluded Claims in 21.3 cover confidentiality, data-protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirm payment obligations are not damages. "Fees" (1.5) is a meaningful base of recurring, professional-services and usage fees.

input.rationale: Vendor gives the full preferred indemnity: IP infringement (20.1) plus breach of law, bodily injury/property damage, Customer Data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud (20.2). Procedure in 20.4 is standard, 20.5 provides procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and Customer's reverse indemnity in 20.3 is narrow (unmodified Customer material and Customer's unlawful use, with Vendor Technology/modification/instruction exclusions). Indemnities also sit outside the liability cap as Excluded Claims.

content.text: Now submitting the remaining findings.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds us; Section 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to build, buy and compete in any field or territory. The only countervailing restraint is the exclusivity language in Section 2.2, which we have addressed under EXCLUSIVITY.

input.quote: Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 imposes full-term exclusive dealing on us for an entire service category with no performance-based exit — our walk-away position. It also contradicts Section 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and Section 12.3 (no exclusivity commitment). We have proposed deleting it, with a narrowed category/12-month/service-level-exit fallback if Vendor needs protection.

input.quote: Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
input.rationale: The MFN runs the wrong way: it obliges us to extend Vendor the best terms we give any other technology supplier, open-endedly and with no product limit or comparison carve-outs — our walk-away position. It also conflicts with the no-most-favoured-customer acknowledgement in Section 12.3. We have proposed deletion.

input.quote: For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
input.rationale: The non-solicit binds only us, runs 18 months post-termination, covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term, bars "engaging" them (an effective no-hire) and has no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. We have narrowed it to the fallback: mutual, 12 months from the end of a person's involvement, involved personnel only, with carve-outs and no no-hire.

input.quote: 9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides only termination for material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2) and our special cause triggers (9.3); there is no termination-for-convenience right anywhere, in a three-year term (Section 8.1). Absence of a Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is our walk-away, so we have inserted a new 9.6 giving us 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund keyed to Section 10.2, and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term.

input.quote: Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
input.rationale: The renewal term (12 months) and the Section 8.3 uplift cap (lesser of CPI and 3%, 90 days' notice) meet our position, but a 180-day non-renewal window exceeds even our walk-away threshold of 90 days. We have shortened the opt-out to 30 days and added a 60-day Vendor renewal reminder; 60 days is our fallback.

input.quote: This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
input.rationale: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County is exactly our preferred position, with no arbitration. CISG is excluded, and the Section 28.3 executive escalation expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings.

input.quote: Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Preferred position met: we may assign to Affiliates and successors without consent (24.1); Vendor may not assign, delegate or transfer by change of control without our consent and never to a competitor (24.2); and 24.4 bars any Vendor termination, suspension, repricing or fee acceleration on our change of control. Section 24.3's catch-all applies only to "other assignments" and does not cut back 24.1, and Section 13.3 aligns licence transfer with Section 24.

input.quote: Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
input.rationale: We own Customer Data and our pre-existing IP (14.1) and each Deliverable, with a present assignment from Vendor and personnel (14.2). Vendor retains only Vendor Technology, backed by the perpetual Section 13.2 licence where embedded (14.3), and 14.4 bars joint ownership and keeps feedback unrestricted for us. The 14.1 "improve the Services" processing right is confined to improving the Services for us and is further constrained by Section 15.1 (no model training or cross-customer combination without consent), so it does not transfer rights in our data.

input.quote: Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer.
input.rationale: Affiliates and contractors are expressly covered (13.1); paid-up and embedded software carries a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence with modification rights (13.2); licence rights transfer to an Affiliate or successor (13.3); and there is no at-will revocation — suspension is limited to a material uncured breach after notice and cure. The Section 13.4 restrictions are conventional and expressly do not limit authorised security testing or use of Customer Data and output.

input.quote: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
input.rationale: Unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems is our walk-away position, and it directly contradicts Section 22.2, which already says Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems. We have limited audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, records-based only and with no system access; the Section 22.2 cost allocation (Vendor pays unless underpayment exceeds 5%) already meets our position.

input.quote: Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: Section 7.6 imposes uncapped liquidated damages on us of USD 25,000 per day triggered by any dependency delay, however minor — our walk-away position, since accrual is unbounded and could exceed the remaining contract value. We have replaced it with schedule relief plus Vendor's documented, reasonable additional time-and-materials costs, and confirmed no penalties are payable by us.

input.quote: Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.
input.rationale: All preferred limits are present (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' compensation), maintained through the term plus one year, with certificates on request under 18.2 and an express statement that insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. No change required.

input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: Preferred position met: no minimum or take-or-pay commitment, fees are payable only for ordered Services, and non-ordering is expressly not a shortfall. Section 12.3 reinforces that we have given no minimum-volume undertaking, and Section 7.1 bars unlisted minimum-use charges. Residual risk is limited to a commitment appearing in a future Order Form, which we will police at that stage.

input.quote: Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form.
input.rationale: Preferred position met in full: six months' transition assistance including migration and cooperation with a replacement supplier (11.1); return of all Customer Data within 30 days in a documented machine-readable format with metadata and no fee-dispute hostage (11.2); and secure deletion only after we confirm successful return, certified by an officer (11.3). Section 10.1 keys the access cut-off to the end of the agreed transition period, so there is no gap.

system.text:
You are customer-side in-house counsel reviewing a contract against an entire playbook in one agent loop.
Use document tools to investigate every rule. Quotes and redline anchors must be verbatim. Keep edits minimal and directionally correct.
For every deviation or missing clause, validate with propose_redline before submit_finding. Submit one finding per rule, then stop.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

messages.content:
Rules:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.


---

ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.


---

ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.


---

ID: EXCLUSIVITY
Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Exclusivity limited to a defined product category and 12 months, ending automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

Position — walk-away:
Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit.
Detection guidance:
Phrases like "exclusive", "sole and exclusive provider", "shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure … from any third party". Exclusivity granted to Customer (e.g. Vendor won't serve our competitors) is acceptable and not a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback; keep any exclusivity that benefits Customer.

---

ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

---

ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

---

ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


---

ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

---

ID: GOVLAW
Title: Governing law and venue
Kind: parametric
Summary: Accepted laws are New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales; courts, not foreign arbitration.
Severity: medium
Category: governing-law
Position — preferred:
Laws of the State of New York; exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County.
Position — fallback:
Delaware or California law and courts; or the laws of England and Wales with the courts of London.
Position — walk-away:
Vendor's home jurisdiction outside the accepted list with exclusive foreign venue, or mandatory arbitration seated abroad.
Detection guidance:
Find the governing-law clause; extract jurisdiction and dispute forum; note any arbitration seat.
Redline guidance:
Replace only the jurisdiction words and forum; keep the rest of the sentence intact.

---

ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

---

ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

---

ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

---

ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

---

ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

---

ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


---

ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


---

ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

---

ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a sole-and-exclusive supplier obligation, and this clause contradicts Sections 2.1 and 12.3, so we have deleted it. If Vendor needs protection we could discuss exclusivity limited to a defined product category for 12 months, ending automatically if Vendor misses service levels.
input.summary: Delete Customer exclusivity obligation in 2.2.

input.comment: [Playbook] We do not give most-favoured-customer undertakings to suppliers, and this clause is inconsistent with Section 12.3, so we have deleted it. MFN pricing running in our favour remains welcome.
input.summary: Delete Customer-side MFN in 7.2.

ops.oldText: Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
ops.newText: If Customer materially delays a dependency identified in an Order Form, Vendor is relieved of the affected obligations and dates for the period of delay and may recover its documented, reasonable additional time-and-materials costs actually incurred as a result. No liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer.

input.comment: [Playbook] We do not pay liquidated damages or penalties; USD 25,000 per day for any dependency delay is punitive and uncapped. We have replaced it with schedule relief plus Vendor's documented additional costs, which is the standard remedy for customer-caused delay.
input.summary: Replace Customer-payable liquidated damages with schedule relief and documented costs.

ops.oldText: unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice
ops.newText: unless either Party gives thirty days' advance written notice before the end of the then-current term, and Vendor shall remind Customer of the upcoming renewal at least sixty days before it occurs

input.comment: [Playbook] A 180-day non-renewal window is far longer than we can operate; our position is a 30-day opt-out with a 60-day Vendor reminder (fallback: 60 days). The 12-month renewal term and the Section 8.3 uplift cap of the lesser of CPI and 3% are acceptable.
input.summary: Shorten non-renewal notice from 180 to 30 days and add renewal reminder.

ops.oldText: For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
ops.newText: For twelve months after a person's involvement in the Services ends, neither Party will knowingly solicit for employment any of the other Party's personnel who were directly involved in performing or receiving the Services. This does not restrict general advertisements or other recruitment not targeted at the other Party's personnel, responses to them, or the hiring of any person who approaches a Party on an unsolicited basis, and neither Party is restricted from hiring any person.

input.comment: [Playbook] We accept only a mutual, narrow non-solicit: 12 months from the end of a person's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire. The 18-month, all-personnel, "engage" restriction binding only us is not acceptable and conflicts with Section 12.3.
input.summary: Make non-solicit mutual, 12 months, involved personnel only, with carve-outs and no no-hire.

ops.oldText: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
ops.newText: No more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice and during normal business hours, Vendor may engage an independent auditor bound by confidentiality obligations to verify Customer's usage of the Services by reviewing relevant usage records Customer provides. Vendor and its auditor have no right of access to Customer's systems, whether remote or on-site.

input.comment: [Playbook] Audits of our usage must be no more than annual, on 30 days' notice, records-based and conducted by an independent auditor, with no access to our systems. As drafted, unlimited unannounced audits with remote system access is a walk-away and already contradicts the access limits in Section 22.2.
input.summary: Limit audits to annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, records only, no system access.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty or early-termination charge, in which case Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination in accordance with Section 10.2. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

input.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 contains no convenience right, which we cannot accept in a three-year term (Section 8.1). We have added a Customer-only termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund keyed to Section 10.2; our fallback is 60-90 days' notice.
input.summary: Insert Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund.

input.rationale: Matches our preferred position: mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees (paid or payable) and USD 1,000,000; mutual consequential-damages exclusion in 21.2 with incident-response and replacement-service costs preserved as direct damages; Excluded Claims in 21.3 cover confidentiality, data-protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirm payment obligations are not damages. "Fees" (1.5) is a meaningful base of recurring, professional-services and usage fees.

input.quote: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Vendor gives the full preferred indemnity: IP infringement (20.1) plus breach of law, bodily injury/property damage, Customer Data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud (20.2). Procedure in 20.4 is standard, 20.5 provides procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and Customer's reverse indemnity in 20.3 is narrow (unmodified Customer material and Customer's unlawful use, with Vendor Technology/modification/instruction exclusions). Indemnities also sit outside the liability cap as Excluded Claims.

content.text: Now submitting the remaining findings.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds us; Section 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to build, buy and compete in any field or territory. The only countervailing restraint is the exclusivity language in Section 2.2, which we have addressed under EXCLUSIVITY.

input.quote: Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 imposes full-term exclusive dealing on us for an entire service category with no performance-based exit — our walk-away position. It also contradicts Section 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and Section 12.3 (no exclusivity commitment). We have proposed deleting it, with a narrowed category/12-month/service-level-exit fallback if Vendor needs protection.

input.quote: Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
input.rationale: The MFN runs the wrong way: it obliges us to extend Vendor the best terms we give any other technology supplier, open-endedly and with no product limit or comparison carve-outs — our walk-away position. It also conflicts with the no-most-favoured-customer acknowledgement in Section 12.3. We have proposed deletion.

input.quote: For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
input.rationale: The non-solicit binds only us, runs 18 months post-termination, covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term, bars "engaging" them (an effective no-hire) and has no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. We have narrowed it to the fallback: mutual, 12 months from the end of a person's involvement, involved personnel only, with carve-outs and no no-hire.

input.quote: 9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides only termination for material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2) and our special cause triggers (9.3); there is no termination-for-convenience right anywhere, in a three-year term (Section 8.1). Absence of a Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is our walk-away, so we have inserted a new 9.6 giving us 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund keyed to Section 10.2, and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term.

input.quote: Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
input.rationale: The renewal term (12 months) and the Section 8.3 uplift cap (lesser of CPI and 3%, 90 days' notice) meet our position, but a 180-day non-renewal window exceeds even our walk-away threshold of 90 days. We have shortened the opt-out to 30 days and added a 60-day Vendor renewal reminder; 60 days is our fallback.

input.quote: This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
input.rationale: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County is exactly our preferred position, with no arbitration. CISG is excluded, and the Section 28.3 executive escalation expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings.

input.quote: Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Preferred position met: we may assign to Affiliates and successors without consent (24.1); Vendor may not assign, delegate or transfer by change of control without our consent and never to a competitor (24.2); and 24.4 bars any Vendor termination, suspension, repricing or fee acceleration on our change of control. Section 24.3's catch-all applies only to "other assignments" and does not cut back 24.1, and Section 13.3 aligns licence transfer with Section 24.

input.quote: Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
input.rationale: We own Customer Data and our pre-existing IP (14.1) and each Deliverable, with a present assignment from Vendor and personnel (14.2). Vendor retains only Vendor Technology, backed by the perpetual Section 13.2 licence where embedded (14.3), and 14.4 bars joint ownership and keeps feedback unrestricted for us. The 14.1 "improve the Services" processing right is confined to improving the Services for us and is further constrained by Section 15.1 (no model training or cross-customer combination without consent), so it does not transfer rights in our data.

input.quote: Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer.
input.rationale: Affiliates and contractors are expressly covered (13.1); paid-up and embedded software carries a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence with modification rights (13.2); licence rights transfer to an Affiliate or successor (13.3); and there is no at-will revocation — suspension is limited to a material uncured breach after notice and cure. The Section 13.4 restrictions are conventional and expressly do not limit authorised security testing or use of Customer Data and output.

input.quote: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
input.rationale: Unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems is our walk-away position, and it directly contradicts Section 22.2, which already says Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems. We have limited audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, records-based only and with no system access; the Section 22.2 cost allocation (Vendor pays unless underpayment exceeds 5%) already meets our position.

input.quote: Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: Section 7.6 imposes uncapped liquidated damages on us of USD 25,000 per day triggered by any dependency delay, however minor — our walk-away position, since accrual is unbounded and could exceed the remaining contract value. We have replaced it with schedule relief plus Vendor's documented, reasonable additional time-and-materials costs, and confirmed no penalties are payable by us.

input.quote: Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.
input.rationale: Meets or exceeds our position: professional and workmanlike services warranty (19.1); 90-day Deliverable conformity running from delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, and hosted Services conformity for the whole subscription term (19.2); no-malicious-code and compliance-with-law warranties (19.3); and a re-perform/repair/replace remedy with a refund and termination backstop that is expressly non-exclusive (19.4). The Section 19.5 disclaimer expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or data-protection duty.

input.quote: Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.
input.rationale: All preferred limits are present (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' compensation), maintained through the term plus one year, with certificates on request under 18.2 and an express statement that insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. No change required.

input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: Preferred position met: no minimum or take-or-pay commitment, fees are payable only for ordered Services, and non-ordering is expressly not a shortfall. Section 12.3 reinforces that we have given no minimum-volume undertaking, and Section 7.1 bars unlisted minimum-use charges. Residual risk is limited to a commitment appearing in a future Order Form, which we will police at that stage.

input.quote: Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form.
input.rationale: Preferred position met in full: six months' transition assistance including migration and cooperation with a replacement supplier (11.1); return of all Customer Data within 30 days in a documented machine-readable format with metadata and no fee-dispute hostage (11.2); and secure deletion only after we confirm successful return, certified by an officer (11.3). Section 10.1 keys the access cut-off to the end of the agreed transition period, so there is no gap.

All 18 rules reviewed and submitted. Summary of our position:

**Deviations requiring redlines (6) — all validated:**

| Rule | Issue | Our edit |
|---|---|---|
| **EXCLUSIVITY** (high) | §2.2 makes Vendor our sole and exclusive hosted-analytics provider for the full term, no performance exit — walk-away, and contradicts §§2.1 and 12.3 | Delete |
| **LD** (high) | §7.6 imposes uncapped USD 25,000/day liquidated damages on us for any dependency delay — walk-away | Replace with schedule relief plus Vendor's documented additional costs |
| **AUDIT** (medium) | §22.1 allows unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems — walk-away, and contradicts §22.2 | Annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, records-based, no system access |
| **RENEWAL** (medium) | §8.2 auto-renews on a 180-day non-renewal window — worse than walk-away | Shorten to 30 days, add 60-day Vendor reminder (§8.3 uplift cap is fine) |
| **NOSOLICIT** (medium) | §12.4 binds only us, 18 months post-termination, all Vendor personnel ever, bars "engaging" (a de facto no-hire), no advertising carve-out | Narrow to mutual/12-month/involved-personnel with carve-outs |
| **MFN** (medium) | §7.2 obliges us to give Vendor our best supplier terms — wrong direction, open-ended | Delete |

**Missing clause (1):** **T4C** — §9 has no convenience right at all in a three-year term (§8.1). We inserted a new §9.6 giving us 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund keyed to §10.2, and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term.

**Compliant (11):** LOL-CAP, INDEMN, NONCOMPETE, GOVLAW, ASSIGN, IP, LICENSE, WARRANTY, INSURANCE, MINCOMMIT, TRANSITION.

Two structural notes worth raising with Vendor: the document contains **duplicate numbering** (two §2.2s and two §7.2s), and in each pair the problematic clause is the inserted one that conflicts with the surrounding drafting — §2.2 (exclusivity) against §§2.1/12.3, §7.2 (MFN) against §12.3, and §22.1 against §22.2. That internal inconsistency supports deletion rather than negotiation on the exclusivity, MFN and audit points.
